A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DriveAgent-R1, with matching authors, core architecture and retained experiments. Inspection of all main-text and appendix pages, including rendered figures, tables and equations, supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original driving-planning evaluations, domain-alignment and training ablations, human evaluations, latency measurements and qualitative cases.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds DriveBench, trajectory-planning and instruction-guided-attention comparisons, plus additional case studies.

M1.justification: v3 Section 3.3 extends the frozen agent with an MLP motion-planning head taking one-hot meta-actions, visual tokens and ego-status to predict three-second trajectories at 2 Hz. This substantially extends v2's high-level action outputs to continuous trajectory prediction. The core hybrid-thinking architecture and cascaded training remain.

E1.justification: v3 adds DriveBench evaluations covering perception, prediction, planning and behavior, and continuous open-loop trajectory prediction on nuScenes. The trajectory task substantially changes output requirements despite reusing an existing dataset. Earlier meta-action and VQA coverage is retained.

E2.justification: New Tables 2–3 compare against DriveLM and Dolphins on DriveBench, and UniAD, VAD-Base, EMMA, DriveVLM-Dual, OmniDrive and OpenDriveVLA (3B) for trajectory planning. Appendix A.13 additionally evaluates instruction-guided attention. The original VLM, human and passive-perception comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: v3 introduces trajectory evaluation with ADE and collision rates at one-, two- and three-second horizons, plus a generic attention-prompt control. Appendix A.7 also revises threshold selection from domain-knowledge justification to iterative VLM/human optimization, retaining the same numerical thresholds. Original splits and principal evaluation settings remain; these descriptions do not establish reruns of retained results.

E4.justification: v3 adds forced-versus-adaptive reasoning comparisons (Figures 14–15), temporal mode-switching demonstrations (Figures 17–18), and quantitative and qualitative tests of active perception versus attention prompting (Table 11 and Figure 19). Earlier ablations remain, and v2's failure case is retained as Figure 16.

E5.justification: Appendix A.7.2 newly describes estimating false-label rates through random human spot-checks during threshold optimization, without reporting audit sizes or uncertainty. The five-run latency procedure remains unchanged, and the new performance comparisons add no confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Original comparison and ablation scores remain unchanged. v3 adds DriveBench results that lead DriveLM on perception and behavior but trail it on prediction and planning; trajectory results with average ADE 0.28 m and collision rate 0.14%; and Table 11 results of 48.81%/44.65% first-frame/sequence accuracy for RoI versus 46.72%/43.83% for instruction-guided attention. These are newly reported comparisons.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a heuristic parameter derivation: assuming one corrected action yields 0.25 gain and amortizing over two calls gives Ctool = 0.125. v2 only supplied an example cost of 0.01. The newly displayed standard GRPO objective is background explanation; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v3 removes the categorical 'first autonomous driving agent' claim from the abstract and 'first to introduce' hybrid thinking from the introduction. The central active-perception, hybrid-thinking, competitive 3B performance and deployment-efficiency contributions otherwise retain their scope.

C2.justification: v3 explains RoI's information gain over attention on downsampled tokens, interprets forced tool use as potentially distracting, and attributes trajectory quality to reasoning-derived meta-actions. These extend the existing interpretations; the visual-overreliance limitation and proposed remedies remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 supplements existing documentation with Drive-Internal retrieval, human screening, maneuver-based selection and 0.5–1.0-second pre-event sampling details. It also documents threshold tuning, the motion-head interface and frozen backbone, and an explicit Ctool of 0.125 instead of v2's 0.01 example. A project-page link is added, without establishing code or data release.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Dolphins, DriveBench, VLM-AD and AutoVLA, using the latter two to contextualize annotation and visual-prompting choices, and removes the DeepSeekMath citation. The related-work discussion and overall active-perception positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose is retained. v3 expands the GRPO explanation, rewrites the labeling discussion, adds experimental and appendix subsections and acknowledgments, and adopts conference headers, lettered appendices and author-date citations. The main narrative is preserved.

P2.justification: v3 adds three tables and five figures featuring side-by-side reasoning comparisons, temporal sequences and an attention-prompt comparison, substantially expanding the visual presentation. Existing figures are retained, including the failure case renumbered from 14 to 16, while tables and page flow are reorganized into conference format.

improvement.justification: DriveBench comparisons and the attention-prompt control provide useful evidence absent from v2, while additional dataset-construction details improve transparency. The trajectory extension also demonstrates downstream applicability. These gains are limited by sparse training details for the new head and the unsupported attribution of its performance specifically to meta-actions without a corresponding ablation. Table 3 also shows a displacement-versus-collision tradeoff, rather than uniformly better planning.
